title: Economics and Indigenous Nations
description: An introduction to economic theory and policy analysis relevant for Indigenous nations in Canada and elsewhere; draws on literature in development economics, health economics, economic history, and labour economics; applies economic principles to policy design in Indigenous contexts; introduces Indigenous research methods to economics students. Provides basic guidance on principles of conduct for working with Indigenous communities. Topics may include an economic history of specific Indigenous nations, self-governance, labour market outcomes and property rights.
notes: May be offered as a joint undergraduate and graduate class.
